messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager: HIGH for customer CASCADE (private VPC). Multiple 401s seen from their Dedicated pool and VPC auth bridge. Incident created INC-2026-143.

alice.m: saw the alert, on it. are we seeing token validation errors or mutual TLS failures?

dmitri.k: logs show OIDC verification failures: `oauth.verify: invalid_kid` and `jwks: key not found for kid=Zx3b7` across gateways in eu-west and us-east. same time window ~15:04 UTC.

carla.ops: customer reports that all API calls requiring auth are failing with 401 since ~15:00. They have a dedicated capacity pool (dedicated-3) and Private VPC with an auth bridge. Impact: control-plane pings ok but auth traffic blocked.

alice.m: confirmed in our metrics: CASCADE tenant auth success rate dropped to 0% at 15:01. other tenants unaffected. sounds like IdP rotated keys but our JWKS cache didn't pick it up.

ben.oncall: pinging CASCADE's IdP now, @idp-support-bot can you confirm recent key rotation event?

idp-support-bot: CASCADE IdP webhook: key rotation completed at 14:59 UTC, new KID Zx3b7 published to https://idp.casade.example/.well-known/jwks.json. No errors reported from IdP side.

alice.m: but our edge caches still have old JWKS (old KIDs). I can see requests hitting our auth cache returning old keys. looks like CDN purge to our JWKS endpoint failed in eu-west.

dmitri.k: digging into auth-bridge logs: `authbridge: jwks-fetch failed: cache-not-updated(304) -> responding with stale keys` then `token verify: kid Zx3b7 not found`. There are also errors from the jwks-fetcher service: `http: 403 while fetching jwks from provisioned origin` for eu-west.

carla.ops: escalation: this is customer-visible; they're on enterprise SLA. paging customer success. I'll start a Zoom if we need bridge.

alice.m: mitigation plan: 1) force JWKS refresh for CASCADE tenant on auth-bridge instances in eu-west/us-east. 2) if refresh fails, temporarily accept tokens signed by previous KID for 30 minutes as a rollback. 3) coordinate with CASCADE IdP to roll back rotation if necessary. 4) postmortem and safer rotation steps.

ben.oncall: can you run the forced refresh endpoint? I have creds. `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://auth-internal.prod/internal/tenants/cascade/refresh-jwks`

dmitri.k: running now from eu-west bastion...

carla.ops: watch logs, I'll notify CASCADE support.

dmitri.k: response: `200 OK {"refreshed": false, "reason": "origin-403"}`. eu-west origin returning 403 when our fetcher tries to pull jwks.

alice.m: that explains it. origin 403 means IdP is blocking our edge agent IPs. maybe they rotate IP allowlist during rotation for security. carla, did CASCADE mention IP restrictions?

carla.ops: confirming with CASCADE: they do have strict allowlist. they were performing rotation inside their firewall and temporarily blocked our fetcher IP for the new JWKS URL unintentionally. they have opened a support ticket with their security team.

ben.oncall: immediate options: A) get CASCADE to temporarily whitelist our fetcher IPs for jwks.json (fastest). B) ask CASCADE to upload the new JWKS into Redwood Console under tenant keystore (requires console action from their admin). C) apply tenant-level emergency bypass to accept previous KID. Which is fastest?

carla.ops: CASCADE can whitelist in ~10-20m. they said they can also paste the JWKS payload into the Console if we give them the admin URL.

alice.m: I'll enable emergency fallback in auth service to accept previous KID for 15 minutes while they fix allowlist. Deploying hotfix to auth-bridge now (patch: add allowed_legacy_kids override per-tenant).

incident-bot: code-deploy started by alice.m for service auth-bridge:deploy/2026-05-14-0843-hotfix (canary 5% -> 100%).

ben.oncall: rolling canary... monitoring traces for auth success.

dmitri.k: canary looks good in us-east. eu-west still sees origin 403 on fetch but token verify returns success when legacy kid allowed. CASCADE confirms traffic is flowing again for some requests.

carla.ops: CASCADE support: we've whitelisted the fetcher IPs. they confirmed our fetcher can now reach https://idp.casade.example/.well-known/jwks.json returning new keys.

alice.m: running manual refresh now after whitelist: `POST /internal/tenants/cascade/refresh-jwks` -> response `200 OK {"refreshed": true, "keys_count": 2}`. auth success rate for tenant back to 99% within 45s.

ben.oncall: nice. stopping emergency legacy-kid acceptance in 5m and reverting the temporary config.

dmitri.k: removing override now and re-validating tokens. success rate stable at 99.8%.

carla.ops: doing customer handoff to support and CSM. CASCADE asked for RCA and next steps: a) we will add monitoring for jwks fetch 403s tied to tenant rotation events. b) add an admin flow to pre-stage new JWKS (upload) before rotation. c) suggest customer whitelist our fetchers or use our upload flow to avoid firewall issues.

alice.m: filing incident ticket INC-2026-143 with timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups. root cause: CASCADE IdP rotated keys while firewall allowlist blocked our JWKS fetcher, causing stale JWKS in our caches that in turn led to token verification failures in the VPC auth bridge and Dedicated pool.

ben.oncall: next oncall: @dmitri.k will take post-incident action items, I'll hand off remaining notes in 30m if anything else crops up.

dmitri.k: acknowledged, I'll own the RCA and the follow-up tasks: (1) implement pre-staging JWKS upload flow, (2) alerting for tenant-specific jwks-fetch 4xx/5xx, (3) update runbook for key rotation with enterprise customers.

carla.ops: CSM on the Zoom with CASCADE now, customer satisfied with temporary fix and waiting for a formal RCA. I'll coordinate communications.

incident-bot: INC-2026-143 STATUS -> mitigated (customer auth restored). Follow-up tasks assigned, severity lowered to SEV3.

alice.m: marking thread for postmortem. thanks everyone, nice quick collaboration. :clap:

ben.oncall: handoff complete.
